Patch 0.33.2 (Repro sandbox QA tooling)

  • Repro sandbox coverage is broader: `repro.html` now includes deterministic dungeon room previews for Verdant, Abyss, Molten, and Tempest themes.
  • Boss approach checks are faster: The sandbox highlights start, reward, `boss_approach`, and boss beats without requiring login, networking, or a live dungeon run.
  • Manual QA has a repeatable route: Added a dedicated 0.33.2 smoke workflow for rendering, movement, VFX, menu chrome, and dungeon pacing checks.
  • Regression coverage: Added coverage for repro controls, live-boot isolation, deterministic dungeon room previews, smoke workflow documentation, and the 0.33.2 release state.

Patch 0.33.1 (Dungeon boss approach pacing)

  • Boss approach beats are now explicit: Dungeon room summaries mark the final traversable room before each boss with boss-approach pacing metadata.
  • Route surfaces call out the commit beat: Objectives, Journal guidance, dungeon entrance hints, minimap markers, world-map previews, and combat callouts now identify Approach rooms before the boss goes live.
  • Rewards and progression stay stable: Boss approach is pacing metadata only, so chest, shrine, elite ambush, boss clear, unlock, and reward behavior remains unchanged.
  • Regression coverage: Added server and client coverage for boss-approach summary metadata, route copy, minimap/world-map markers, entrance hints, combat callouts, and the 0.33.1 release state.

Patch 0.33.0 (Mesh catalog expansion)

  • Procedural enemy definitions are now catalog-owned: Fire, air, and water realm enemy silhouettes now live in MeshCatalog instead of MeshFactory.
  • Renderer behavior stays unchanged: MeshFactory still exposes the same procedural spec entry point and uses the same generated geometry, tint, emissive, scale, cache, hitbox, and fallback behavior.
  • Future content additions are safer: New procedural enemy definitions can be added through catalog data without editing the factory's runtime creation flow.
  • Regression coverage: Added coverage for cataloged procedural enemy specs, representative realm and dungeon silhouettes, and MeshFactory compatibility with the catalog-owned table.

Patch 0.32.4 (Keybind clarity settings)

  • Control Hints are now adjustable: Settings adds a Standard controls / Detailed keyboard reference selector.
  • Help can now expand keyboard guidance: Detailed mode adds grouped movement, combat, navigation, and camera shortcut reminders to the Help screen.
  • Input behavior stays unchanged: The setting only changes Help presentation and persists as `eidolon.controlHintLevel`.
  • Regression coverage: Added coverage for control-hint persistence, invalid-value normalization, Help presentation toggling, settings markup, and the 0.32.4 release state.

Patch 0.32.3 (UI scale baseline)

  • UI Scale is now adjustable: Settings adds an 85% to 125% UI Scale slider for menus and HUD text.
  • The preference persists safely: UI scale is stored as `eidolon.uiScale`, normalizes invalid values back to 100%, and updates the visible percentage immediately.
  • Viewport safety stays intact: Scaling applies through the shared UI layer so existing viewport-capped windows keep their screen bounds and scroll behavior.
  • Regression coverage: Added coverage for UI scale persistence, clamping, DOM presentation, CSS scale tokens, and the 0.32.3 release state.

Patch 0.32.2 (Audio asset readiness)

  • Authored cue slots are now defined: The shared AudioManager exposes replacement-ready `.ogg` and `.mp3` metadata for every UI, loot, combat, and jump cue.
  • Generated sounds remain the safe fallback: Missing or unavailable authored media falls back to the existing generated cue layer instead of breaking feedback.
  • Playback stays centralized: Optional authored media uses the same cue route, volume, mute, detail-level, and cooldown rules as synthesized sounds.
  • Regression coverage: Added coverage for cue asset metadata, authored media playback, generated fallback behavior, and the 0.32.2 release state.

Patch 0.32.1 (Audio detail controls)

  • Audio detail is now adjustable: Settings adds an Audio Detail selector with Full cues and Reduced UI cues modes.
  • Reduced UI cues quiets routine menu noise: UI click and window open/close sounds are suppressed while gameplay feedback like loot, combat, and jump sounds remains available.
  • The control persists with the shared audio manager: Audio detail uses the same centralized settings path as audio enablement and volume.
  • Regression coverage: Added coverage for reduced-detail filtering, invalid detail-level normalization, UIManager persistence, settings presentation, and the 0.32.1 release state.

Patch 0.32.0 (Audio foundation)

  • The first audio layer is live: A client-owned AudioManager now provides generated placeholder cues that can later be replaced with authored audio assets.
  • Moment-to-moment feedback now has sound: UI clicks and window open/close actions, loot pickup and inventory-full feedback, combat hits and misses, and jump takeoff and landing all route through the shared audio manager.
  • Audio controls are available in Settings: Players can toggle audio cues and adjust synthesized cue volume, with preferences persisted between sessions.
  • Regression coverage: Added coverage for audio defaults and cue definitions, loot success/failure cues, combat hit/miss cues, jump start/landing cues, settings presentation, and the 0.32.0 release state.

Patch 0.31.41 (Client UX closeout)

  • The final 0.31 UI pass closes the remaining overlay chrome gap: The death/respawn overlay now uses reusable CSS classes and shared button styling instead of inline layout and hover rules.
  • Death recovery presentation now follows the viewport-safe client baseline: Title, guidance, metadata, and respawn action sizing clamp for small screens while keeping the recovery copy readable.
  • The roadmap is ready for 0.32: 0.31 is marked closed for planned client-UX consistency work, making the next active slice the 0.32 audio foundation.
  • Regression coverage: Added closeout coverage for death overlay classes, removed inline death-screen chrome, 0.31.41 version presentation, and the 0.32-ready roadmap state.

Patch 0.31.40 (Viewport-safe window layout)

  • Window placement now runs through shared viewport rules: Primary menus, service windows, support modals, and the world map reflow through one managed layout path instead of each surface fighting for screen space.
  • Inventory companions now respect available width: Shop, Stash, and Forge keep Inventory beside them on wide screens, but narrow viewports prioritize the service window so full contents stay visible instead of overlapping.
  • HUD and tooltip surfaces are safer on small screens: Objectives gain a capped scroll lane, player HUD/mobile offsets avoid fixed offscreen positions, and tooltips clamp back into the viewport.
  • Regression coverage: Added coverage for managed menu exclusivity, wide-versus-narrow service companions, full-frame drag clamping, layout CSS guardrails, and 0.31.40 version presentation.
